source_title: Macfarlane Group PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 35, 54, 65 and 97 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 27 February 2020; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Macfarlane delivered steady growth despite weaker demand and price deflation in parts of Packaging Distribution. Group profit before tax rose to £12.0m, Packaging Distribution gross margin improved to 31.1% from 29.5%, Manufacturing Operations profit increased despite a broadly stable 38.2% margin, net bank debt fell to £12.7m and all covenants were met. Enfield and a small manufacturing site had already closed, while continued property-footprint consolidation was an ordinary efficiency priority.
already_announced_exclusion: The Enfield and Nether Broughton site closures and associated transfers were completed in 2019 and are excluded from any future target event; ordinary property consolidation, logistics efficiency and acquisition integration are also excluded.
review_note: Contained demand and property-cost pressure is outweighed by profit growth, margin improvement, lower debt and covenant compliance; no unresolved qualifying intervention signal was identified.

source_title: Macfarlane Group PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 47, 86 and 120 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 24 February 2022; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: COVID disruption, supply shortages, staffing costs and significant input-price inflation persisted, with some end markets still below pre-pandemic levels. Macfarlane nevertheless increased revenue to £264.5m, profit before tax to £18.7m, operating margin to 7.6% and gross margin to 33.8%; operating cash inflow was £23.8m, net bank funds were £2.5m and severe downside testing retained sufficient liquidity and covenant headroom. Manufacturing returned to profit after restructuring undertaken in H2 2020.
already_announced_exclusion: The H2 2020 Manufacturing restructuring, Labels disposal and announced Wigan/Manchester site consolidation were already undertaken or public before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Inflation, supply and staffing pressure is credible but contained; revenue, profit, margin, cash, net-funds and downside-liquidity evidence provide dominant quantified offsets.

source_title: Macfarlane Group PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 39 and 45 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 29 February 2024; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Normalising e-commerce demand, sales-price deflation and slower industrial markets reduced Group revenue 3% to £280.7m and Packaging Distribution revenue 6%, while operating costs rose 4%. Effective input-price management lifted Group gross margin to 37.6% from 33.8%, adjusted operating margin rose to 9.8% from 8.6%, adjusted profit before tax increased 10% to £25.8m and operating cash inflow rose to £33.5m, leaving £0.5m of net bank funds after acquisitions and investment.
already_announced_exclusion: No qualifying restructuring or equivalent intervention had been announced by cutoff; routine sales, logistics and administrative efficiency programmes, acquisition integration and historic property changes are excluded from the target definition.
review_note: Clear demand and operating-cost pressure is more than offset by margin expansion, profit growth, strong cash generation, net funds and covenant compliance; no unresolved intervention signal was identified.
